abstract: A caller posing as a courier (FedEx/DHL) says a parcel linked to the victim's Aadhaar contains drugs and has been seized by customs; the call is transferred to a fake 'police station' where a uniformed officer places the victim under 'digital arrest' on video, isolates them, and over hours/days pressures them to transfer funds to a 'verification account' to prove innocence.
safe_verification_channel: disconnect and call the local police (112) or cyber-crime helpline 1930 directly; Indian agencies never arrest over a video call

abstract: A caller claiming to be from the telecom regulator (TRAI) tells the victim that multiple criminal complaints have been registered against their mobile number and it will be disconnected; the call escalates to fake police who threaten arrest unless the victim 'verifies' by transferring money.
safe_verification_channel: TRAI/telecom never call to threaten disconnection over complaints; hang up and verify with your operator's official app

abstract: A caller says a parcel in the victim's name contains illegal items (credit cards, drugs) and that an FIR has been filed; posing as customs/police they demand immediate payment to a 'safe account' to clear the victim's name.
safe_verification_channel: courier companies and customs never ask for payment by phone; call the official courier number and police 1930
